summary: Tested Trek Booking Platform (backend + frontend), Laws page search, and chat code-syntax highlighting. Backend: 19/19 pytest tests passed (list, filters, detail, bookings CRUD with auth, review validation & creation). Frontend: trek grid renders 8 cards, search/difficulty/country/sort filters work, empty state shown for nonsense; trek detail opens, itinerary accordion toggles, pax +/- updates total ($2,980 -> $4,470 for 3 pax @ Everest). Guest booking submit shows toast and redirects to /auth. Logged-in admin booked Langtang, was navigated to /trek/bookings, cancel button flipped booking to cancelled. Review posted (4-star) appears in reviews list. Laws search filters 14 docs, 'sovereignty' shows 4 matches with citations, nonsense shows laws-search-empty, clear restores 14 docs. Chat code highlighting: CodeBlock renders with dark theme, PYTHON label, colored token spans, working copy button flips to 'copied!' after click.
critical_code_review_comments: trek.py list_treks: uses case-insensitive $regex without escaping user input; benign for read-only but consider re.escape() for defensive style.

trek.py create_booking: no upper bound check for departure_date being in the past — currently only verifies membership in trek['departures']; seeded dates are future so safe, but future seasons should filter past dates.
TrekDetail.jsx: booking submit does not disable the button until user/date/etc validated client-side; relies on server 400 (works correctly).
